name: Star
description: 'Star' is the record that put King Akeem on the map, and the numbers behind it are not subtle. King Akeem, a CWI roster artist, has pushed the single past 112,000 plays, turning a local favorite into the calling card of the wider CWI catalog. Co-produced by Black, the track shows its construction in every choice: a sturdy, uncluttered beat that keeps the full frame on the vocals, trap drums with room to breathe, and a hook built for maximum carry. The mix runs bass-heavy throughout, with booming 808s under the verses, a deep bassline holding the low end, and open hi-hats ringing out in the chorus, while layered ad-libs give the hook its call-and-response lift. A heavy snare cracks in the chorus, and muted keys carry the melody underneath, keeping the arrangement celebratory without ever sounding crowded. The genre is straight-ahead rap and hip hop with a pop rap reach — anthemic, triumphant, and confident, trading avant-garde edges for raw celebratory force. King Akeem raps like a man reporting from the top of the climb: defiant about the distance traveled, serious about what comes next, and hype in the way only a true breakout feels. For fans of pop rap with real momentum, 'Star' recalls the catalog's most aggressive celebrations, and it sits in conversation with the alternative rap lane that raised it. It sits alongside the roster's defining singles as the record that traveled on word of mouth before the algorithms noticed — entering Radio 365's rotation in 2026, where the hook has done the same work everywhere else: made a room full of strangers say the title back. Euphoric and unapologetic, it sounds like a coronation that never ended.
